h: Wurlitzers, steam and the north Norfolk countryside
p: The collection is at Thursford, a little village between Fakenham and Holt, so you'll want a car for this one. It's well worth the drive along the quiet country lanes, and it's the sort of place that fits perfectly into a few days exploring north Norfolk.

One of the treasures here is a mighty Wurlitzer organ, the kind that once rose up in front of audiences in grand old cinemas. Hearing one played is an experience in itself, with a richness of sound you just don't get from a recording. Keep an ear out, because music is a big part of what makes Thursford so special.

How long to spend? Allow a couple of hours to look at the exhibits properly, read the stories and enjoy the music. Steam fans and anyone with family links to the old travelling fairs could happily stay longer. Take your time and look closely at the painted panels, carved figures and gleaming brass work. Every piece was built to dazzle.

There's plenty more to do in the area. Holt is a handsome Georgian town packed with independent shops and cafés. Wells-next-the-Sea has a lovely sandy beach backed by pine woods and a row of colourful beach huts, and Little Walsingham, with its historic shrines and quiet streets, is a short drive away. Pensthorpe Natural Park near Fakenham is another good choice for families who like wildlife and outdoor play.
North Norfolk's coast is also brilliant for seal trips and crabbing, so a museum visit can easily become the start of a wider weekend.
